title: Small Text at 3 mm sews as a running line, as PE-DESIGN's SR fonts do
description: Hello 0123 in OpenStitch Line at 3 mm, against the numbers recorded from PE-DESIGN 11.50's Small Text font 04 Utah SR at 3.0 mm (round 8, #530). PE-DESIGN's file is a Brother font's output, so it stays in the owner's notes and never in the repository: only its recorded numbers are used here, as expected values (internal-regression tier, not reference). Compared: the height (both fonts are 3 mm), that it is a running line (no satin), and no trim inside a letter. Not compared, and recorded only: PE-DESIGN's 22.5 mm width and 165 stitches belong to its own wider Utah font (OpenStitch Line is 16.0 mm, 63 stitches at its 1.5 mm pitch), and its about 8 trims between letters are a deliberate difference (OpenStitch joins letters on a line by running stitch up to 1.2 x the size).

evidence.note: PE-DESIGN 11.50 Small Text, font 04 Utah SR, 3.0 mm, Hello 0123: 22.5 x 3.2 mm, 165 stitches, a running line, about 8 trims (coordinator's round-8 capture, numbers on #530; the file is not in the repository)

measurements.evidence: PE-DESIGN's Utah SR at 3.0 mm is 3.2 mm high (round 8, #530)
PE-DESIGN's SR (running) Small Text fonts sew a running line, no satin: every stitch short (round 8, #530); OpenStitch Line's pitch is 1.5 mm
#530's acceptance: trims only between letters farther apart than 2 mm; this line's letters are joined by running stitch (PE-DESIGN trims about 8 times here, a deliberate difference)
